solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Confusion about river creature dwelling by water

indicators.note: the confusion word wraps around the river letter, as one thing goes about another

parts.note: a fog is a state of mental confusion

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer is muddled about some animal living at the river's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The frog is an amphibian that lives in and beside ponds and streams.

clue.text: Working in resin, living alone

indicators.note: the word for working is placed within the resin word

parts.note: mastic is a resin from the mastic tree
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Someone toiling away with resin, leading a solitary existence.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks live a secluded, solitary life apart from the world, which is what monastic describes.

clue.text: Little outlaw's put on rug upside-down

indicators.note: in a down clue, the outlaw word placed on top of the rug word sits above it

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning the rug word upside down reads it bottom to top

parts.note: a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: A small criminal has been laid on an overturned carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' looks like an adjective for the outlaw but is the definition. 'upside-down' turns MAT into TAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of chicken, so the word is used for anything diminutive.

clue.text: Soldiers start to tremble in deluge? Definitely

parts.note: a force is a body of soldiers

indicators.note: the opening of tremble sits within the deluge word

parts.note: a deluge is a heavy downpour of rain

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Troops begin to shake in a flood? There's no doubt about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Said of something known without doubt, an adverb phrase equal in meaning to surely.

clue.text: Young fellow in stage work, not old character

indicators.note: the young fellow is placed within the trimmed stage work
not old means the old letter is left out of the stage work

parts.note: an opera is a work for the stage
a son is a young male offspring

explanation.surface: A youth appears in a theatrical production, though not an old character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' deletes the old letter from the stage work before the young fellow is placed inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A persona is a role or assumed character, as an actor or writer adopts.

clue.text: Creep in front line

parts.note: the prow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone sneaking forward while in the front rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To prowl is to move stealthily, like a predator stalking, which is creeping about.

clue.text: Made amends, bringing in witness, confused and perplexed

indicators.note: the amends word takes the other letters into its middle

parts.note: to atone is to make amends

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone apologised by calling a witness, and was left baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made amends' looks like the definition, but it supplies the outer letters; 'confused' jumbles witness, and 'bringing in' places the jumble inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at one's wits' end is an idiom for being utterly baffled and at a loss.

clue.text: Flying back, taking in Lima and Quito finally

indicators.note: the back word takes the other letters inside itself

parts.note: aft means at the back of a ship
Lima is the NATO alphabet word for L

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: An air traveller returning home after visiting two South American capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima and Quito look like the cities, but Lima is the radio code for L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aloft is high up in the air, as a bird or plane in flight is.

clue.text: Note is stuck up in restaurant passage

indicators.note: the note and the turned word sit within the restaurant word

parts.note: a trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant

indicators.note: in a down clue, stuck up means the little word reads from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A notice has been pinned up inside a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck up' turns IS into SI; TRAT is short for trattoria.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of passing across or through, a passage from one place to another.

clue.text: Arcade game's first I start to admire, chasing record

indicators.note: the record comes first and the other letters follow behind it

parts.note: a log is a written record

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of game, and the lone I gives itself
the start of the admire word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A gamer marvels at the start of a game while pursuing a high score.
explanation.definitionFit: A loggia is an open gallery or arcade along the side of a building.

clue.text: One should improve spying and agree to participate when probed by spies

indicators.note: the spies push their way inside the agreeing word

parts.note: to opt in is to agree to take part
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: An agent who should sharpen their espionage agrees to join when questioned by the secret service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spying' here just means seeing, not espionage.
explanation.definitionFit: An optician tests eyesight and prescribes lenses to help people see better.

clue.text: Closely follow fielders with side bagging runs

parts.note: slips are fielders beside the wicketkeeper in cricket

indicators.note: the side word captures the runs letter inside it

parts.note: a side is a team
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket captain shadows the fielders while the team piles on runs.
explanation.walkthrough: Slips are cricket fielders standing next to the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: To slipstream is to travel just behind another vehicle, using its wake.

clue.text: Writer, having problem, securing way out with little resistance

indicators.note: the problem word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a plight is a difficult situation

indicators.note: out signals the letters of way are put out of order

parts.note: R is the physics abbreviation for resistance

explanation.surface: An author in difficulty finds an escape route with hardly any opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way out' reads as an exit, but 'out' signals jumbling the letters of way; 'securing' puts them, plus R, inside the problem word.
explanation.definitionFit: A playwright is a dramatist, someone who writes plays.

clue.text: Crowd heading off in a hurry

indicators.note: the head of the crowd word comes off, losing its first letter

parts.note: a crush is a dense crowd

explanation.surface: A mob sets off at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush job is one done in a hurry, so rush serves as a modifier for haste.

clue.text: Police document crash we brought about in forthright style

indicators.note: brought about suggests turning things round, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: arrant means downright or out-and-out

explanation.surface: Officers write up a smash-up we caused, in blunt language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' rearranges CRASH WE into SEARCHW.
explanation.definitionFit: A search warrant is a legal document authorising police to search premises.

clue.text: Posed problem with a fruit

parts.note: a model who posed sat for the artist
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A puzzle was set involving a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a kind of mandarin orange, a citrus fruit.

clue.text: Tough equipment letting in water after top's removed

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: something porous lets water through

explanation.surface: Hard-wearing kit that leaks once its lid is taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: POROUS loses its top letter to give OROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigorous means strict and demanding, as tough standards are.

clue.text: Awkward situation less enthusiastic politicians recalled

indicators.note: recalled, read as called back, means the word is written backwards

parts.note: wets were moderate Conservatives lukewarm about Thatcherite policies

explanation.surface: Half-hearted MPs are brought back into an embarrassing predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: Wets were moderate Tory MPs in the Thatcher era.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is an idiom for being in a state of anxiety or trouble.

clue.text: I oppose resolution of stagnation

indicators.note: resolution, as breaking something into parts, means these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone objects to ending a period of economic stagnation.
explanation.definitionFit: An antagonist is an opponent, someone who could say of their rival that they oppose them.

clue.text: Start to lose initial shade

indicators.note: the word loses its initial letter

parts.note: the dawning of an era is its start

explanation.surface: A painter begins to lose the first coat of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canopy that gives shade from the sun.

clue.text: Bridge crossing current in country

indicators.note: the bridge word crosses over and encloses the current letter

parts.note: to bridge a gap is to span it
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A bridge spans a flowing stream somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a nation of the Iberian peninsula in Europe.

clue.text: Clear soup in summer month — that's about right

indicators.note: the month goes about the right word, surrounding it

parts.note: June is a summer month in the northern hemisphere
a lien is a legal right to hold another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A chef serves a light broth in midsummer, and that seems correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Julienne is a clear soup with thin strips of vegetables.

clue.text: Sword cut absorbed by scoundrel? Try again

indicators.note: the shortened sword is taken into the scoundrel word

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person

indicators.note: cut means the sword word is shortened by a letter

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: A villain was struck by a blade, so attempt the attack once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat an action is to do it again or have another go.

clue.text: Run and hide

definitions.meaning: an animal's skin with the fur on

explanation.definitionFit: Pelt means both to dash along at speed and the fur-covered skin of an animal.

clue.text: A glow emitting a little energy will become pale

indicators.note: emitting means giving out, so the energy letter leaves the glow word

parts.note: a sheen is a soft glow
E is the physics abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: Something giving off light while losing power will turn wan.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means grey like ashes, the colour of a face drained of blood.

clue.text: Beat floor-covering, removing last ridge

parts.note: to drum is to beat repeatedly

indicators.note: the floor-covering word loses its final letter

parts.note: lino is short for linoleum

explanation.surface: Pound the rug, but take the end piece off.
explanation.definitionFit: A drumlin is a long glacial mound or ridge of clay.
